tutorial.en:
# Pan

The camera pans (rotates horizontally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **pan** pivots the camera left or right on a fixed axis without physically displacing the camera body.

Panning is one of the most fundamental and frequently used camera movements in filmmaking, used to **survey a scene, follow lateral action, connect two subjects, or reveal off-screen space**. It ranges from slow, contemplative sweeps across a landscape to rapid whip-pans that serve as energetic transitions.

The term "pan" derives from "panorama," reflecting the movement's original purpose of capturing wide scenic views.

- Related: [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10) | [Truck](taxonomy:5)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜

相机在任意方向进行摇镜（水平旋转），可能同时伴随其他运动。**摇镜**是相机在固定轴上左右旋转，而不改变相机的物理位置。

摇镜是电影制作中最基础、最常用的相机运动之一，用于**扫视场景、跟随横向运动的主体、连接两个主体，或展示画面外的空间**。它是横移（Truck）的旋转对应物：摇镜旋转而横移位移。由于摇镜不引入视差，它呈现出更「平面」的视觉效果，但执行起来更简单，且不需要推轨或移动平台。

甩镜（Whip Pan）——极快速的摇镜导致画面模糊——是一种常见的风格化技法，用于场景之间的过渡或制造突发的能量爆发。

- 相关: [摇镜左](taxonomy:8) | [摇镜右](taxonomy:10) | [横移](taxonomy:5)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Left

The camera only pans leftward without any other camera movement. A **pan** is a horizontal rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, sweeping the frame from right to left. Unlike a [Truck Left](taxonomy:6), the camera body stays in place and simply pivots.

Filmmakers use pan left to **follow a subject moving screen-left, reveal new information beside the current frame, or shift the audience's attention** from one part of a scene to another. A slow pan left can build anticipation, while a fast whip-pan creates an energetic transition.

The pan is one of the oldest deliberate camera movements, dating to the earliest days of cinema when operators hand-cranked cameras on tripod heads. Today it remains a fundamental building block of visual storytelling.

- Related: [Pan Right](taxonomy:10) | [Truck Left](taxonomy:6)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜左

相机仅向左摇镜，没有其他运动。**摇镜**是相机在固定轴上进行水平旋转，将画面从右向左扫过。与[横移左](taxonomy:6)不同，相机本身不移动，只是旋转。

电影创作者使用向左摇镜来**跟随向画面左方移动的主体、揭示当前画面旁边的新信息，或将观众注意力从场景的一个部分转移到另一个部分**。摇镜的速度传达不同的效果：缓慢的摇镜营造沉思和审视的感觉，中速摇镜跟随动作，而快速甩镜则作为场景之间的过渡或制造突发的运动冲击。

- 相关: [摇镜右](taxonomy:10) | [横移左](taxonomy:6)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Right

The camera only pans rightward without any other camera movement. A **pan** is a horizontal rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, sweeping the frame from left to right. Unlike a [Truck Right](taxonomy:12), the camera body stays in place and simply pivots.

Filmmakers use pan right to **follow a subject moving screen-right, survey a landscape, or guide the viewer's eye** toward a new point of interest. In Western cultures, where reading flows left-to-right, a rightward pan can feel natural and progressive.

- Related: [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Truck Right](taxonomy:12)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜右

相机仅向右摇镜，没有其他运动。**摇镜**是相机在固定轴上进行水平旋转，将画面从左向右扫过。与[横移右](taxonomy:12)不同，相机本身不移动，只是旋转。

电影创作者使用向右摇镜来**跟随向画面右方移动的主体、扫视风景或将观众的视线引导向新的关注点**。在阅读方向从左到右的文化中，向右摇镜在感知上可能更顺畅、更自然，而向左摇镜则可能带有微妙的逆行或回溯感。

- 相关: [摇镜左](taxonomy:8) | [横移右](taxonomy:12)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt

The camera tilts (rotates vertically) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **tilt** angles the camera up or down on a fixed axis without physically raising or lowering the camera body.

Tilting is used to **reveal vertical space, follow rising or falling action, survey tall structures, or shift between a character's face and hands**. It is the vertical counterpart of the pan and equally fundamental to camera grammar.

- Related: [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Pedestal](taxonomy:36)
tutorial.zh:
# 俯仰

相机在任意方向进行俯仰（垂直旋转），可能同时伴随其他运动。**俯仰**是相机在固定轴上向上或向下改变角度，而不物理升高或降低相机本体。

俯仰用于**展示垂直空间、跟随上升或下落的动作、扫视高大建筑物，或在角色的面部和双手之间切换视线**。它是摇镜的垂直对应物，同样是相机语法中最基础的运动之一。

- 相关: [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [升降](taxonomy:36)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Up

The camera only tilts upward without any other camera movement. A **tilt** is a vertical rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, angling the lens upward while the camera body remains stationary. Unlike a [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) or [Crane Up](taxonomy:4), the camera does not physically rise.

Filmmakers tilt up to **reveal height, convey power or grandeur, or follow a subject rising**. A classic use is the slow tilt up a skyscraper facade to emphasize scale. In character work, tilting up from feet to face can build mystery or introduce a figure with dramatic weight.

Alfred Hitchcock and Orson Welles frequently used exaggerated tilt angles to create psychological tension, pairing tilt with low-angle framing.

- Related: [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Crane Up](taxonomy:4)
tutorial.zh:
相机仅向上仰拍，没有其他相机运动。**上仰**是相机在固定轴上将镜头向上旋转，而相机本身不升高。与[升降上升](taxonomy:38)或[摇臂上升](taxonomy:4)不同，相机不进行物理位移。

电影制作者使用上仰来**展示高度、传达力量感或宏伟感，或跟随上升的主体**。

- 相关: [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [升降上升](taxonomy:38) | [摇臂上升](taxonomy:4)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Down

The camera only tilts downward without any other camera movement. A **tilt** is a vertical rotation of the camera on a fixed axis, angling the lens downward while the camera body remains stationary. Unlike a [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) or [Crane Down](taxonomy:3), the camera does not physically descend.

Filmmakers tilt down to **reveal what lies below the current frame, show a character's point of view looking downward, or create a sense of vulnerability**. A slow tilt down from sky to ground can establish setting, while a sudden tilt down can direct attention to a critical detail on the floor or table.

- Related: [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
相机仅向下俯拍，没有其他相机运动。**下俯**是相机在固定轴上将镜头向下旋转，而相机本身不下降。与[升降下降](taxonomy:32)或[摇臂下降](taxonomy:3)不同，相机不进行物理位移。

电影制作者使用下俯来**揭示当前画面下方的内容、展示角色向下看的视角，或营造脆弱感**。

- 相关: [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [升降下降](taxonomy:32) | [摇臂下降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Roll

The camera rolls (rotates around the optical axis) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **roll** tilts the horizon line by rotating the entire frame clockwise or counterclockwise.

Roll is among the most disorienting camera movements and is used sparingly for **dream sequences, psychological disturbance, point-of-view shots from a tumbling character, or stylized transitions**.

- Related: [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:82)
tutorial.zh:
# 横滚

相机在任意方向进行横滚（绕光轴旋转），可能同时伴随其他运动。**横滚**通过绕镜头光轴旋转整个画面来使地平线倾斜。

横滚在电影中使用较为稀少，因为它直接挑战观众的空间定向感，但正是这种特性使其成为传达**梦境、心理失衡、醉酒状态或风格化转场**的有力工具。持续的横滚可以营造天旋地转的效果，而缓慢的微横滚则能增添一丝不安的暗流。

- 相关: [顺时针横滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针横滚](taxonomy:16)

tutorial.en:
# Roll Clockwise

The camera only rolls clockwise without any other camera movement. A **roll** rotates the camera around its optical axis (the line from lens to subject), tilting the horizon line. Clockwise roll causes the frame's horizon to rotate so the left side rises and the right side dips.

Roll is used sparingly because it breaks the audience's sense of spatial orientation. Filmmakers employ it to **convey disorientation, dream states, or a character's altered perception**. A sustained roll can suggest the world turning upside down, while a quick snap-roll can punctuate a moment of shock.

The Dutch angle (or canted angle) is a related but distinct concept: it is a static tilt of the frame, whereas a roll is a continuous rotation. Some filmmakers transition from a Dutch angle into a roll to intensify unease.

- Related: [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:83)
tutorial.zh:
# 顺时针横滚

相机仅顺时针横滚，没有其他运动。**横滚**是相机绕光轴（从镜头到主体的连线）旋转，使地平线倾斜。顺时针横滚使画面左侧上升、右侧下降。

横滚因打破观众的空间定向感而被谨慎使用。电影创作者运用它来**传达迷失方向感、梦境状态或角色感知的改变**。持续的横滚可以暗示世界在天翻地覆，而快速的急旋横滚则能为震惊时刻画龙点睛。

荷兰角（倾斜角度）是相关但不同的概念：荷兰角是静态的画面倾斜，而横滚是持续的旋转运动。一些电影创作者会从荷兰角过渡到横滚，以逐步加强不安感。

- 相关: [逆时针横滚](taxonomy:16) | [荷兰角](taxonomy:82)

tutorial.en:
# Roll Counterclockwise

The camera only rolls counterclockwise without any other camera movement. A **roll** rotates the camera around its optical axis, tilting the horizon line so the right side rises and the left side dips.

Like clockwise roll, this movement conveys **disorientation or dreamlike instability**. Counterclockwise roll is sometimes chosen for its subtly different visual rhythm, or to match the direction of an on-screen rotation (a falling character, a spinning object).

- Related: [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:83)
tutorial.zh:
# 逆时针横滚

相机仅逆时针横滚，没有其他运动。**横滚**是相机绕光轴旋转，使地平线倾斜，右侧上升、左侧下降。

与顺时针横滚一样，这一运动传达**迷失方向感或梦幻般的不稳定感**。逆时针横滚有时因其微妙不同的视觉节奏而被选用，或用于匹配画面中旋转的方向（坠落的角色、旋转的物体）。

- 相关: [顺时针横滚](taxonomy:14) | [荷兰角](taxonomy:82)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom

The camera zooms (changes focal length) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **zoom** magnifies or widens the view without physically moving the camera, changing the field of view while keeping the camera's position fixed.

Zooms alter framing without introducing parallax, giving them a distinctive "flat" quality compared to dolly movements. They are used to **draw attention to a detail, create dramatic emphasis, or smoothly reframe within a continuous shot**.

- Related: [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly](taxonomy:33)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦

相机在任意方向进行变焦（改变焦距），可能同时伴随其他运动。**变焦**通过改变焦距来放大或缩小视野，而相机本身的位置保持不变。

变焦改变画面构图时不会引入视差，因此呈现出与推拉运动截然不同的「平面」质感。变焦常用于**聚焦细节、制造戏剧张力，或在连续镜头中平滑地重新构图**。

- 相关: [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [推拉](taxonomy:33)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom In

The camera only zooms in with no other movement. A **zoom** changes the lens focal length, magnifying the center of the frame without physically moving the camera. The result narrows the field of view and brings distant subjects closer.

Unlike a [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35), a zoom does not change the camera's physical position, so the perspective relationship between foreground and background objects stays the same. This gives zooms a distinctive "flat" feel compared to the parallax shift of a dolly.

Zooms became ubiquitous in the 1960s and 1970s with directors like Robert Altman and Sergio Leone, who used long, creeping zooms to isolate characters or objects. Stanley Kubrick's slow zoom in [*Barry Lyndon* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Lyndon) and the snap-zoom in [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) are celebrated examples.

- Related: [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦推进

相机仅进行变焦推进，没有其他运动。**变焦推进**通过改变镜头焦距放大画面中心，而相机本身不移动。视野收窄，远处主体被拉近。

与[推轨前进](taxonomy:35)不同，变焦推进不改变相机的物理位置，因此前景与背景之间的透视关系保持不变。这赋予变焦一种独特的「平面」感，区别于推轨的视差效果。

变焦在1960至1970年代随罗伯特·奥特曼和塞尔吉奥·莱昂内等导演而广泛应用。斯坦利·库布里克在[《巴里·林登》(1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Lyndon)中的缓慢变焦，以及[《闪灵》(1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film))中的骤然推进，都是影史经典。

- 相关: [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [推轨前进](taxonomy:35) | [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Zoom Out

The camera only zooms out with no other movement. A **zoom out** widens the lens focal length, expanding the field of view and making the subject appear to recede into a broader context.

Filmmakers use zoom outs to **reveal surroundings, create a sense of isolation, or transition from an intimate detail to a wider establishing view**. A slow zoom out from a character's face can suggest emotional distance or loneliness, while a rapid zoom out can deliver a comedic or shocking reveal of unexpected scale.

- Related: [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 变焦拉远

相机仅进行变焦拉远，没有其他运动。**变焦拉远**扩大镜头焦距，拓展视野，使主体看似退入更广阔的环境之中。

电影创作者使用变焦拉远来**揭示周围环境、营造孤立感，或从亲密细节过渡到宏观全景**。从角色面部缓缓拉远可暗示情感的疏离；而骤然拉远则能制造喜剧或惊悚式的规模揭示。

- 相关: [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [推轨后退](taxonomy:29) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Truck

The camera trucks (translates laterally) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **truck** physically displaces the camera left or right, producing parallax between foreground and background elements.

Trucking creates a more immersive, three-dimensional feel than panning because the physical displacement reveals depth relationships in the scene. It is essential for **tracking lateral movement, creating flowing compositions, and building spatial awareness**.

- Related: [Truck Left](taxonomy:6) | [Truck Right](taxonomy:12) | [Pan](taxonomy:7)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移

相机在任意方向进行横移（横向平移），可能同时伴随其他运动。**横移**（Truck，又称横向推轨）使相机整体向左或向右进行物理位移，在前景和背景元素之间产生视差。

横移比摇镜营造出更具沉浸感的三维效果，因为物理位移揭示了场景中的深度关系。它对于**跟踪横向运动、创造流畅构图和建立空间感知**至关重要。

- 相关: [横移左](taxonomy:6) | [横移右](taxonomy:12) | [摇镜](taxonomy:7)

tutorial.en:
# Truck Left

The camera only moves physically leftward without any other camera movement. A **truck** (also called a **tracking shot** or **crab**) translates the entire camera body sideways along a horizontal axis. Unlike a [Pan Left](taxonomy:8), which merely pivots, a truck physically displaces the camera, producing parallax between foreground and background objects.

Filmmakers use truck left to **follow a subject walking screen-left, reveal depth in a scene, or create a flowing lateral composition**. Because trucking introduces real parallax, it feels more immersive and three-dimensional than a pan.

Historically, truck shots required dolly tracks or wheeled platforms. Modern stabilizers (Steadicam, gimbals) and drones have made smooth lateral movement far more accessible.

- Related: [Truck Right](taxonomy:12) | [Pan Left](taxonomy:8)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移左

相机仅向左进行物理横移，没有其他运动。**横移**（又称**推轨**或**蟹行**）使相机整体沿水平轴向侧方平移。与[摇镜左](taxonomy:8)仅旋转不同，横移使相机进行物理位移，在前景和背景物体之间产生视差。

电影创作者使用向左横移来**跟随向画面左方移动的主体、展示场景的深度层次，或创造流畅的横向构图**。由于横移引入了真实的视差效果，因此比摇镜更具沉浸感和立体感。

历史上横移需要推轨铁轨或轮式平台。现代稳定器（斯坦尼康、云台）和无人机使平滑的横向运动变得更加易于实现。

- 相关: [横移右](taxonomy:12) | [摇镜左](taxonomy:8)

tutorial.en:
# Truck Right

The camera only moves physically rightward without any other camera movement. A **truck right** translates the camera body to the right, creating parallax between foreground and background elements. Unlike a [Pan Right](taxonomy:10), the camera physically moves rather than pivoting.

Truck right shares the same cinematic applications as truck left: **following lateral subject movement, revealing spatial depth, and composing dynamic lateral shots**. The direction is chosen to match the subject's motion or the desired reveal direction.

- Related: [Truck Left](taxonomy:6) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10)
tutorial.zh:
# 横移右

相机仅向右进行物理横移，没有其他运动。**横移右**将相机整体向右平移，在前景和背景元素之间产生视差效果。与[摇镜右](taxonomy:10)仅旋转不同，横移涉及相机的物理位移。

向右横移在视觉感受上是向左横移的镜像，用于**跟随向画面右方移动的主体、扫视场景，或创造与画面内运动相匹配的横向构图**。推拉方向的选择通常取决于场景的场面调度需求。

- 相关: [横移左](taxonomy:6) | [摇镜右](taxonomy:10)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly

The camera dollies (translates forward or backward) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **dolly** physically moves the camera closer to or farther from the scene, changing perspective through real spatial displacement.

Dolly movement is distinct from zooming: it introduces parallax (foreground objects shift relative to background), creating a natural depth effect that zooms cannot replicate. This makes dollying the preferred technique for **intimate character moments, dramatic reveals, and immersive forward progression**.

- Related: [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Zoom](taxonomy:21)
tutorial.zh:
# 推拉

相机相对地面进行前后推拉运动（推轨），可能同时伴随其他运动。**推拉**通过物理位移使相机靠近或远离场景，通过真实的空间位移改变透视关系。

推拉运动与变焦有本质区别：推拉引入视差（前景物体相对背景发生位移），创造出变焦无法复制的自然深度效果。这使得推拉成为**亲密的角色时刻、戏剧性揭示和沉浸式前进推进**的首选技法。

- 相关: [推轨前进](taxonomy:35) | [推轨后退](taxonomy:29) | [变焦](taxonomy:21)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Forward

The camera only moves physically forward (not zoom in) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **dolly in** pushes the camera closer to the subject, compressing the apparent distance between foreground and background through natural parallax.

Unlike a [Zoom In](taxonomy:22), which magnifies without moving the camera, a dolly forward changes perspective: foreground objects grow faster than background objects, drawing the viewer into the scene. This depth-driven immersion is why dollying is often preferred over zooming for dramatic moments.

The dolly dates to the silent era; D.W. Griffith is often credited with early dolly experiments. The invention of the Western Dolly in the 1930s and the Steadicam in 1975 vastly expanded how filmmakers could execute forward movement.

- Related: [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29) | [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 推轨前进

相机仅相对地面向前进行物理移动（非变焦推进），没有其他运动。**推轨前进**（Dolly In）使相机靠近主体，通过自然视差压缩前景与背景之间的距离感。

与[变焦推进](taxonomy:22)不同，推轨前进改变了相机的物理位置，因此引入了视差效果：前景物体相对背景移动更快，创造出将观众拉入场景的感觉。这种透视变化赋予推轨前进一种变焦无法复制的沉浸感和「呼吸感」。

推轨前进是叙事电影中最常用的摄影运动之一。从适度前推跟随角色行走到缓慢、毫米级精确推进逐渐揭示情感，它的运用范围极为广泛。斯坦利·库布里克的缓慢正面推进和斯皮尔伯格的快速紧急推进各自定义了一种导演风格。

- 相关: [推轨后退](taxonomy:29) | [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Backward

The camera only moves physically backward (not zoom out) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **dolly out** pulls the camera away from the subject, expanding the visible environment and revealing the broader context around the subject.

Filmmakers use dolly backward to **create emotional distance, reveal isolation, or widen from an intimate moment to a larger scene**. A slow dolly out at the end of a scene is a classic way to signal closure or reflection.

- Related: [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 推轨后退

相机仅相对地面向后进行物理移动（非变焦拉远），没有其他运动。**推轨后退**（Dolly Out）使相机远离主体，扩展可见环境并揭示主体周围更广阔的背景。

电影创作者使用推轨后退来**营造情感距离、揭示孤立感、从亲密时刻扩展到宏大场景，或创造离别和告别的视觉隐喻**。从角色面部缓缓后退可以暗示情感疏离或无力感，而从紧密构图拉开至广阔环境则能制造壮观的环境揭示。

- 相关: [推轨前进](taxonomy:35) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal

The camera pedestals (translates vertically) relative to the ground, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **pedestal** physically raises or lowers the camera while maintaining its angle, unlike a tilt which pivots in place.

Pedestal movement creates a clean vertical shift in vantage point, used to **follow rising or descending subjects, adjust camera height for different shot sizes, or create smooth vertical reveals** without the angular change of a tilt or the arcing path of a crane.

- Related: [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Tilt](taxonomy:19)
tutorial.zh:
# 升降

相机相对地面进行垂直升降运动（升降平移），可能同时伴随其他运动。**升降**在保持相机角度不变的情况下，物理地升高或降低相机位置。与俯仰（原地旋转）不同，升降是真正的位移。

升降运动产生干净的垂直视角变化，用于**跟随上升或下降的主体、为不同景别调整相机高度，或创造平稳的垂直揭示效果**，且不会产生俯仰的角度变化或摇臂的弧线路径。

- 相关: [升降上升](taxonomy:38) | [升降下降](taxonomy:32) | [俯仰](taxonomy:19)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal Up

The camera only moves physically upward (not tilt up) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **pedestal up** (or **boom up**) raises the camera vertically while maintaining its angle, unlike a [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) which pivots in place, or a [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) which arcs along a curved path.

Filmmakers pedestal up to **follow a rising subject, gradually reveal overhead elements, or shift the camera's vantage point from a low angle to a higher perspective**. The movement maintains a constant viewing angle to the ground, producing a clean vertical translation without the perspective rotation of a tilt.

- Related: [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32) | [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Crane Up](taxonomy:4)
tutorial.zh:
# 升降上升

相机仅相对地面向上进行物理移动（非上仰），没有其他运动。**升降上升**（又称 Boom Up）在保持相机角度不变的情况下垂直升高相机。与[上仰](taxonomy:20)（原地旋转）或[摇臂上升](taxonomy:4)（沿弧线路径移动）不同。

电影创作者使用升降上升来**跟随上升的主体、调整相机高度以适应不同的景别需求、创造从低位到高位的平滑垂直揭示效果**，同时保持地平线稳定。该运动产生纯粹的垂直位移，不带有俯仰的角度变化或摇臂的弧形路径。

- 相关: [升降下降](taxonomy:32) | [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [摇臂上升](taxonomy:4)

tutorial.en:
# Pedestal Down

The camera only moves physically downward (not tilt down) relative to the ground without any other camera movement. A **pedestal down** (or **boom down**) lowers the camera vertically while maintaining its angle, unlike a [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) or [Crane Down](taxonomy:3).

Filmmakers pedestal down to **follow a descending subject, lower the camera to a child's or pet's eye level, or shift from an elevated vantage to ground level**. The movement preserves the camera's angular orientation, keeping horizon lines steady.

- Related: [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 升降下降

相机仅相对地面向下进行物理移动（非下俯），没有其他运动。**升降下降**（又称**摇臂下降** Boom Down）在保持相机角度不变的情况下垂直降低相机。与[下俯](taxonomy:18)或[摇臂下降](taxonomy:3)不同。

电影创作者使用升降下降来**跟随下降的主体、将相机降至儿童或宠物的视平线高度，或从架高视角过渡到地面视角**。该运动保持相机的角度朝向不变，使地平线保持稳定。

- 相关: [升降上升](taxonomy:38) | [下俯](taxonomy:18) | [摇臂下降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom

The camera performs a dolly zoom effect (combining physical dolly movement with simultaneous opposing zoom) in any direction. The **dolly zoom** (also called the **Vertigo effect**) produces a distinctive warping of background perspective while keeping the subject roughly the same size in frame.

First popularized by Alfred Hitchcock in [*Vertigo* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film)), the technique conveys **psychological realization, shock, or disorientation**. It has since appeared in iconic scenes in [*Jaws* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film)) and [*The Lord of the Rings* (2001)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)).

- Related: [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25) | [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦

相机执行滑动变焦效果（将物理推拉运动与同步反向变焦相结合）。**滑动变焦**（又称**眩晕效果**）在保持主体大致相同大小的同时，产生背景透视的独特扭曲。

由阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克在[《迷魂记》(1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film))中首次推广，此技术传达**心理觉醒、震惊或迷失方向感**。

- 相关: [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25) | [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom In

The **dolly zoom in** (also called the **Vertigo effect**) combines a forward dolly movement with a simultaneous zoom out. The background appears to stretch away from the subject, producing a strong sense of **spatial unease**. A common variant keeps the subject roughly the same size in frame while the background warps dramatically around them.

Filmmakers use this technique to convey **psychological realization, shock, or disorientation** — making it a go-to tool for moments of sudden emotional shift. First popularized by Alfred Hitchcock in [*Vertigo* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film)), the effect has since appeared in iconic scenes in [*Jaws* (1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film)) and [*The Lord of the Rings* (2001)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series)).

- Related technique: [Dolly Zoom Out](taxonomy:26)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦推进

**滑动变焦推进**（又称**眩晕效果**、**Vertigo 效果**）将向前推轨运动与同步变焦拉远相结合。背景看起来从主体身后急剧拉伸，产生强烈的**空间不安感**。常见变体是让主体在画面中保持大致相同的大小，而背景则围绕其发生剧烈扭曲。

电影创作者使用此技法来传达**心理顿悟、震惊或迷失方向感**——使其成为突发情绪转变时刻的标志性手段。该效果由阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克在[《迷魂记》(1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertigo_(1958_film))中首度推广，此后在[《大白鲨》(1975)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaws_(film))和[《指环王》(2001)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings_(film_series))的标志性场景中均有出现。

- 相关技法: [滑动变焦拉出](taxonomy:26)

tutorial.en:
# Dolly Zoom Out

The camera performs a dolly zoom effect with backward movement and zoom-in. This is the **reverse Vertigo effect**: the camera pulls backward while simultaneously zooming in, keeping the subject roughly the same size but causing the **background to appear to compress and close in** behind them.

Where the [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25) stretches the background away to convey shock or realization, the dolly zoom out pushes the background forward, creating a sense of **claustrophobia, entrapment, or mounting pressure**. The technique can make a space feel like it is shrinking around the subject.

Though less commonly used than its forward counterpart, the reverse dolly zoom appears in films like [*Goodfellas* (1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), where Martin Scorsese used it in the famous diner scene to suggest paranoia closing in.

- Related: [Dolly Zoom In](taxonomy:25)
tutorial.zh:
# 滑动变焦拉出

相机执行滑动变焦效果——向后推轨的同时变焦推进。这是**反向眩晕效果**：相机后退而镜头推进，保持主体在画面中大致相同的大小，但使**背景看起来被压缩并向主体逼近**。

与[滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)拉伸背景以传达震惊不同，滑动变焦拉出将背景推向前方，营造**幽闭感、被困感或压力倍增**的视觉效果。这种技法能让空间本身仿佛在主体周围收缩。

虽然不如正向变体常见，反向滑动变焦在[《好家伙》(1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)的经典餐厅场景中有精彩运用，马丁·斯科塞斯以此暗示偏执感正在逼近。

- 相关: [滑动变焦推进](taxonomy:25)

tutorial.en:
# Arc

The camera arcs (orbits) around the subject in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. An **arc shot** moves the camera along a curved path around a subject while keeping the subject in frame.

Filmmakers use arc shots to **add visual dynamism, reveal multiple sides of a subject, convey psychological tension, or emphasize a pivotal moment in dialogue**. Famous arc shots include the circling camera in [*Goodfellas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas) and the bullet-time orbit in [*The Matrix* (1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix).

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1) | [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2)
tutorial.zh:
# 弧形

相机沿弧形路径绕主体运动（环绕镜头），可能同时伴随其他相机运动。

电影制作者使用弧形镜头来**增加视觉动感、展示主体多个侧面、传达心理张力**。著名范例包括[《好家伙》](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)和[《黑客帝国》(1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix)的子弹时间。

- 相关: [顺时针弧形](taxonomy:1) | [逆时针弧形](taxonomy:2)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Clockwise

The camera arcs clockwise around the subject. An **arc shot** (or **orbit shot**) moves the camera along a curved path around a subject while keeping the subject in frame. Clockwise means the camera travels to the right as seen from above.

Filmmakers use arc shots to **add visual dynamism, reveal multiple sides of a subject, convey psychological tension, or emphasize a pivotal moment in dialogue**. A slow arc can create intimacy and dimensionality, while a fast orbit can heighten drama or disorientation. The arc also reveals depth in a scene by continuously changing the parallax relationship between subject and background.

Famous arc shots include the circling camera in the restaurant scene of [*Goodfellas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), and the iconic 360-degree orbit in [*The Matrix* (1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix) (achieved with the bullet-time rig).

- Related: [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2)
tutorial.zh:
相机顺时针绕主体做弧形运动。**弧形镜头**（或**环绕镜头**）沿弧形路径绕主体移动。顺时针指从上方看相机向右移动。

电影制作者使用弧形镜头来**增加视觉动感、展示主体多个侧面、传达心理张力或强调对话中的关键时刻**。著名的弧形镜头包括[《好家伙》](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)餐厅场景和[《黑客帝国》(1999)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Matrix)的子弹时间。

- 相关: [逆时针弧形](taxonomy:2)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Counterclockwise

The camera arcs counterclockwise around the subject. An **arc shot** moves the camera along a curved path around a subject. Counterclockwise means the camera travels to the left as seen from above.

Arc direction is typically chosen to match blocking, reveal key background elements at the right moment, or complement the emotional arc of the scene. Counterclockwise arcs can feel subtly different in rhythm from clockwise ones, and directors often choose direction based on which side of the subject they want to reveal first.

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1)
tutorial.zh:
# 逆时针弧形

相机逆时针绕主体做弧形运动。**弧形镜头**沿曲线路径绕主体移动。逆时针指从上方看相机向左方移动。

弧形方向通常根据场面调度来选择，以在恰当的时机揭示关键的背景元素，或配合场景的情感弧线。逆时针弧形与顺时针弧形在视觉节奏上有微妙的差异，导演往往根据希望首先揭示主体的哪一侧来选择方向。

- 相关: [顺时针弧形](taxonomy:1)

tutorial.en:
# Crane

The camera cranes (moves along a curved vertical arc) in any direction, potentially combined with other simultaneous camera movements. A **crane shot** uses a jib or crane arm to move the camera along an arcing vertical path, simultaneously changing height and viewing angle.

Crane shots are used for **sweeping reveals, establishing geography, and creating a sense of transcendence or descent**. They date to the 1930s and became iconic through films like [*Gone with the Wind* (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film)).

- Related: [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) | [Crane Down](taxonomy:3)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇臂

相机沿弧形垂直路径做摇臂运动，可能同时伴随其他相机运动。

摇臂镜头用于**全景展示、建立地理环境和营造超越或下沉感**。经典案例包括[《乱世佳人》(1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film))。

- 相关: [摇臂上升](taxonomy:4) | [摇臂下降](taxonomy:3)

tutorial.en:
# Crane Up

The camera cranes upward in an arc relative to its own frame. A **crane up** moves the camera along a curved vertical path, typically pivoting on a jib or crane arm. Unlike a straight [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38), the crane produces an arcing trajectory where the camera simultaneously rises and changes its viewing angle.

Filmmakers use crane up shots for **sweeping reveals, establishing geography from above, and creating a sense of liberation or transcendence**. A crane up at the end of a scene often conveys release, escape, or an emotional widening of perspective.

Crane shots date to the 1930s with early mechanical jibs, but became iconic through films like [*Gone with the Wind* (1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film)), which featured a legendary crane-up over wounded soldiers in Atlanta. Modern telescoping cranes and drone rigs can achieve even more dramatic vertical arcs.

- Related: [Crane Down](taxonomy:3) | [Pedestal Up](taxonomy:38)
tutorial.zh:
相机沿弧形路径向上升起。**摇臂上升**沿曲线垂直路径移动，相机同时升高并改变视角。与直线[升降上升](taxonomy:38)不同。

电影制作者使用摇臂上升来进行**全景展示、从高处建立地理环境，以及营造解放或超越感**。经典案例包括[《乱世佳人》(1939)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gone_with_the_Wind_(film))中俯瞰伤兵的摇臂上升。

- 相关: [摇臂下降](taxonomy:3) | [升降上升](taxonomy:38)

tutorial.en:
# Crane Down

The camera cranes downward in an arc relative to its own frame. A **crane down** follows a curved descending path, simultaneously lowering the camera and adjusting its angle. Unlike a straight [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32), the arcing motion adds a sweeping quality.

Filmmakers use crane down to **descend into a scene, move from an establishing overview to an intimate ground-level perspective, or create a feeling of descending weight or gravity**. Opening a scene with a crane down from above can elegantly transition from context to character.

- Related: [Crane Up](taxonomy:4) | [Pedestal Down](taxonomy:32)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇臂下降

相机相对自身画面沿弧形路径向下做摇臂运动。**摇臂下降**沿曲线下行路径移动，同时降低相机高度并调整视角。与直线下降的[升降下降](taxonomy:32)不同，摇臂下降遵循弧形轨迹，因为相机安装在起重机臂的末端。

电影创作者使用摇臂下降来**进入场景、从全景概览平滑过渡到地面亲密视角，或营造重力下沉和降临的感觉**。摇臂下降常用于镜头开场——从高处的建立镜头缓缓降落至角色中间。

- 相关: [摇臂上升](taxonomy:4) | [升降下降](taxonomy:32)

tutorial.en:
# Fast Moving Camera

The camera has noticeable motion at a fast speed. **Fast camera movement** creates energy, urgency, and kinetic excitement. It can convey a character's rush, the chaos of an action sequence, or the exhilaration of speed.

Directors like Michael Bay and the Russo Brothers use rapid camera movement as a signature style in action filmmaking. Fast pans (whip pans) are also used as **transitions** between scenes or time periods, snapping from one composition to the next.

- Related: [Slowly Moving Camera](taxonomy:59) | [Motion Blur](taxonomy:40)
tutorial.zh:
# 快速运动相机

相机以快速速度进行明显运动。**快速相机运动**创造出能量感、紧迫感和动态的运动冲击力。它可以传达角色的匆忙、动作场面的混乱或速度带来的兴奋感。

迈克尔·贝和罗素兄弟将快速相机运动作为动作片拍摄的标志性风格。快速摇镜（甩镜）也被用作场景或时间段之间的**过渡手段**，从一个构图迅速甩向下一个。

- 相关: [慢速运动相机](taxonomy:59) | [运动模糊](taxonomy:40)

tutorial.en:
# Slowly Moving Camera

The camera has noticeable motion at a slow speed. **Slow camera movement** builds atmosphere, draws attention to subtle details, and creates a contemplative or suspenseful mood. A creeping dolly or a glacial pan forces the audience to absorb the frame gradually.

Directors like Andrei Tarkovsky and Terrence Malick are known for extended slow camera movements that evoke meditative or dreamlike states. Stanley Kubrick's slow Steadicam tracking in [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) built unbearable tension through deliberate, unhurried forward motion.

- Related: [Fast Moving Camera](taxonomy:56) | [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61)
tutorial.zh:
# 慢速运动相机

相机以慢速进行明显运动。**慢速相机运动**营造氛围、引导观众关注细微细节，创造沉思或悬疑的情绪。缓慢而深思熟虑的运动给画面赋予庄重和优雅的气质。

斯坦利·库布里克在[《闪灵》(1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film))中的缓慢斯坦尼康跟踪镜头——穿越空旷酒店走廊的幽灵般的滑行——是经典范例。塔可夫斯基的长镜头中近乎静止的缓慢运动同样定义了一种独特的电影语言，使时间本身变得可触可感。

- 相关: [快速运动相机](taxonomy:56) | [平稳运动](taxonomy:61)

tutorial.en:
# Smooth Motion

The video has exceptionally smooth and highly stable camera movement. **Smooth motion** is typically achieved with a Steadicam, gimbal, dolly track, or slider. The absence of vibration keeps the audience's attention on the subject and composition rather than the camera itself.

The Steadicam, invented by Garrett Brown in 1975, revolutionized cinema by enabling smooth, fluid movement through complex environments. Its debut in [*Rocky* (1976)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_(film)) and [*The Shining* (1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film)) demonstrated that a camera could glide through spaces with an almost ghostly precision.

- Related: [Shaky Motion](taxonomy:60) | [Completely Still](taxonomy:57)
tutorial.zh:
# 平稳运动

视频中相机运动极其平稳流畅。**平稳运动**通常通过斯坦尼康、电子云台、推轨或滑轨实现，消除了手持拍摄的有机抖动。

斯坦尼康由加雷特·布朗于1975年发明，彻底改变了电影摄影。在[《洛奇》(1976)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_(film))和[《闪灵》(1980)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Shining_(film))中的首次亮相展示了相机可以以近乎幽灵般的精确度在空间中滑行，跟随角色穿过复杂的环境而不产生任何抖动或颠簸。现代电子云台使这种平稳度在更小型、更经济的设备上成为可能。

- 相关: [抖动运动](taxonomy:60) | [完全静止](taxonomy:57)

tutorial.en:
# Shaky Motion

The video shows noticeable vibrations, shaking, or wobbling of the camera. **Shaky camera work** (or shaky-cam) can be intentional or incidental. When used deliberately, it conveys **raw immediacy, documentary realism, or a character's subjective agitation**.

The technique gained mainstream prominence through films like [*Saving Private Ryan* (1998)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan), where Janusz Kaminski's handheld cinematography placed viewers in the visceral chaos of combat. The found-footage genre ([*The Blair Witch Project*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blair_Witch_Project), [*Cloverfield*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloverfield)) relies on shaky motion as its core aesthetic.

- Related: [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61) | [Handheld Shake](taxonomy:58)
tutorial.zh:
# 抖动运动

视频中相机有明显的振动、抖动或晃动。**手持抖动**（Shaky-Cam）可以是有意的也可以是偶然的。当刻意运用时，它传达**原始的即时感、纪录片式的真实感或角色的主观焦躁**。抖动暗示着有一个真实的人在操作相机，打破了电影制作中第四面墙式的隐形感。

该技法通过[《拯救大兵瑞恩》(1998)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saving_Private_Ryan)的诺曼底登陆场景获得主流认可，摄影师雅努什·卡明斯基的手持拍摄将观众投入战场的混乱之中。保罗·格林格拉斯在《谍影重重》系列中将手持抖动推向极致，使其成为动作片的标志性风格。

- 相关: [平稳运动](taxonomy:61) | [手持微抖](taxonomy:58)

tutorial.en:
# Completely Still

The video shows a completely still camera with no motion or shaking. A **locked-off camera** is mounted on a tripod (or other rigid support) with no movement at all. This is the most neutral camera state, directing all attention to what happens within the frame.

Directors like Wes Anderson and Yasujiro Ozu are celebrated for their disciplined use of static frames. Anderson's symmetrical compositions and Ozu's low-angle tatami shots derive much of their visual power from the camera's absolute stillness, letting composition and blocking carry the storytelling.

- Related: [Handheld Shake](taxonomy:58) | [Smooth Motion](taxonomy:61)
tutorial.zh:
# 完全静止

视频中相机完全静止，没有任何运动或抖动。**锁定机位**（Locked-Off）的相机安装在三脚架或其他固定支架上，绝对不动。这是运动谱系的零点——有意选择的静止。

完全静止的构图将所有视觉注意力集中于**场景本身的内部运动**——演员的表演、光线的变化、环境中的动态——而非相机的运动。韦斯·安德森和小津安二郎以对静态画面的严谨使用而闻名。安德森的对称构图和小津的低角度榻榻米镜头，其视觉力量很大程度上来自相机的绝对静止，使画面如同精心安排的画作。

- 相关: [手持微抖](taxonomy:58) | [平稳运动](taxonomy:61)

tutorial.en:
# Handheld Shake

The video has a mostly stationary camera with only minor vibrations or shaking. **Handheld shake** falls between a locked-off tripod shot and deliberate shaky-cam. The camera is largely still but exhibits the subtle, organic tremor of a human operator.

This look is common in **dialogue-driven dramas and documentaries**, where it adds a sense of presence and immediacy without the disorienting intensity of full shaky-cam. Many cinematographers intentionally shoot handheld even on static setups to inject a subtle sense of life into the frame.

- Related: [Completely Still](taxonomy:57) | [Shaky Motion](taxonomy:60)
tutorial.zh:
# 手持微抖

视频中相机基本静止，仅有轻微的振动或抖动。**手持微抖**介于锁定三脚架拍摄和刻意手持抖动之间。相机基本保持稳定，但存在操作者手持产生的**细微有机颤动**。

这种效果在**对话驱动的剧情片和纪录片**中极为常见，它增添一丝人类临场感和生命力，但不会像全手持抖动那样引起注意或造成视觉不适。许多观众甚至不会察觉到手持微抖的存在，但它在潜意识层面增强了画面的真实感和亲近感。

- 相关: [完全静止](taxonomy:57) | [抖动运动](taxonomy:60)

tutorial.en:
# Tracking Shot

The camera tracks the subject as they move. A **tracking shot** follows a moving subject through space, keeping them in frame as they walk, run, drive, or otherwise travel. The camera may translate, pan, tilt, or combine movements to maintain the subject's position in the composition.

Tracking shots are among the most versatile tools in filmmaking, used to **build intimacy with a character, sustain tension across a continuous take, or immerse the audience in the subject's journey**. The technique can feel invisible when executed smoothly, or deliberately conspicuous as a bravura long take.

One of the most celebrated tracking shots in cinema history is the Copacabana scene in [*Goodfellas* (1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas), where the camera follows Henry and Karen through a restaurant's back entrance in a single unbroken shot. Orson Welles' opening crane-track in [*Touch of Evil* (1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_of_Evil) set the standard for virtuoso tracking.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 跟踪镜头

相机跟随正在移动的主体，使其始终保持在画面中。**跟踪镜头**在主体行走、奔跑、驾驶或以其他方式移动时紧随其后，相机可能通过平移、摇镜、俯仰或组合运动来维持主体在构图中的位置。

跟踪镜头是电影制作中最灵活的工具之一，用于**与角色建立亲密感、在连续长镜头中维持张力，或让观众沉浸在主体的旅程之中**。该技法可以在流畅执行时近乎隐形，也可以作为炫技长镜头刻意引人注目。

影史上最著名的跟踪镜头之一是[《好家伙》(1990)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodfellas)中的科帕卡巴纳场景，相机以一个不间断的长镜头跟随亨利和凯伦穿过餐厅后门。奥逊·威尔斯在[《历劫佳人》(1958)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touch_of_Evil)中的开场起重机跟踪镜头则奠定了炫技跟踪的标杆。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Lead Tracking Shot

A lead tracking shot where the camera moves ahead of the subject, traveling in the same direction as they approach the camera. The camera faces the subject and retreats before them, keeping the subject's face (or front) visible.

Lead tracking is essential for **dialogue scenes in motion, character introductions, and moments where the audience needs to read the subject's expression**. By showing the subject head-on while they advance, the shot creates a sense of direct engagement between character and viewer. It can also build anticipation: the viewer sees where the character is headed only when the camera finally reveals the background.

The technique is common in Steadicam work, where the operator walks backward ahead of the actor.

- Related: [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 前引跟踪

前引跟踪镜头中，相机在主体前方移动，与主体同向行进，面向主体后退拍摄。相机对着主体的正面（或前方），保持主体面部（或正面）可见。

前引跟踪对于**运动中的对话场景、角色介绍，以及需要读取主体表情的时刻**至关重要。通过在角色前进时正面展示其面貌，该镜头在角色与观众之间建立了直接的互动感。它还能制造悬念：观众只有在相机最终揭示背景时才能看到角色前方的景象。

该技法在斯坦尼康拍摄中十分常见，摄影师在演员前方倒退行走。

- 相关: [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Follow Tracking Shot

A follow tracking shot where the camera moves behind the subject, traveling in the same direction as they move away from the camera. The camera sees the subject's back and follows them into the scene.

Follow shots create a feeling of **accompanying the character on their journey**. The viewer shares the character's forward momentum and discovers the environment at the same pace. This perspective is widely used in action sequences, walk-and-talk scenes, and horror films where the unseen threat is implied by the camera's position behind the character.

The Dardenne brothers are known for extended follow shots that stay glued to a character's back, creating visceral intimacy.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:47)
tutorial.zh:
# 后随跟踪

后随跟踪镜头中，相机在主体后方移动，与主体同向行进，拍摄主体的背影并跟随其进入场景。

后随镜头营造出**陪伴角色旅程**的感觉。观众与角色共享前进的动力，以相同的节奏发现周围环境。这一视角广泛用于动作场景、边走边谈的对话场景，以及恐怖片中——相机位于角色身后暗示着看不见的威胁。

达内兄弟以紧贴角色背部的长时间后随镜头闻名，营造出发自肺腑的亲密感。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Side Tracking Shot

A side tracking shot with the camera moving from the side to follow the moving subject. The camera travels parallel to the subject's path of motion, keeping them in profile.

Side tracking is a staple of **dialogue walks, running sequences, and any scene requiring sustained lateral movement**. The profile view lets the audience observe both the subject and the environment passing behind them. It often conveys a sense of progression or journey.

Classic side tracking shots run along dolly rails laid parallel to a street or corridor. Modern gimbals and vehicle rigs allow longer and more dynamic lateral tracks.

- Related: [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50)
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪

侧面跟踪镜头中，相机从侧面跟随移动的主体。相机与主体的运动路径平行移动，保持侧面视角。

侧面跟踪是**对话行走、奔跑场景和任何需要持续横向运动**场景的标准用法。侧面视角让观众能同时观察主体和其身后经过的环境，营造出行进或旅程的感觉。

经典的侧面跟踪镜头沿着与街道或走廊平行铺设的推轨进行拍摄。现代云台和车载设备使得更长、更灵活的横向跟踪成为可能。

- 相关: [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50)

tutorial.en:
# Aerial Tracking Shot

An aerial tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject from an aerial view. The camera is positioned high above, typically from a drone or helicopter, and moves to keep the subject in frame as they traverse the landscape below.

Aerial tracking shots provide a **god's-eye perspective on movement through space**, revealing geography, terrain, and the subject's relationship to their surroundings in ways ground-level shots cannot. They are commonly used in chase sequences, travel montages, and establishing shots of characters moving through expansive environments.

Once requiring expensive helicopter rigs, aerial tracking has become far more accessible with consumer and cinema drones since the 2010s.

- Related: [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52) | [Drone POV](taxonomy:165)
tutorial.zh:
# 空中跟踪

空中跟踪镜头中，相机从高空俯瞰并跟随移动的主体。相机通常安装在无人机或直升机上，从高处保持主体在画面中。

空中跟踪提供**上帝视角的运动透视**，揭示地理地形以及主体与周围环境的关系，这是地面镜头无法实现的效果。该技法常用于追逐场景、旅途蒙太奇和展示角色穿越广阔环境的建立镜头。

空中跟踪拍摄曾经需要昂贵的直升机设备，自2010年代消费级和电影级无人机普及后变得更加容易实现。

- 相关: [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52) | [无人机视角](taxonomy:165)

tutorial.en:
# Arc Tracking Shot

An arc tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject while arcing around them. The camera simultaneously tracks the subject's movement and orbits around them, combining lateral travel with a curved path.

This creates a **highly dynamic, three-dimensional feel** that reveals both the subject and their environment from shifting angles. Arc tracking shots are used for **dramatic confrontations, dance sequences, and action set-pieces** where the filmmaker wants to maintain continuous visual engagement while showing multiple facets of the scene.

- Related: [Arc Clockwise](taxonomy:1) | [Arc Counterclockwise](taxonomy:2) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 弧形跟踪

弧形跟踪镜头中，相机在跟随移动主体的同时绕其做弧形运动。相机同时进行横向跟踪和弧形环绕，将平移与曲线路径相结合。

这创造出**极具动感的三维效果**，从不断变化的角度展示主体和环境。弧形跟踪镜头用于**戏剧性对抗、舞蹈场景和动作大场面**，使电影创作者在保持连续视觉互动的同时展示场景的多个层面。

- 相关: [顺时针弧形](taxonomy:1) | [逆时针弧形](taxonomy:2) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Pan Tracking Shot

The camera pans to track the moving subjects. Rather than translating through space, the camera stays in one position and **rotates horizontally to follow the subject's movement** across the frame.

Pan tracking is the simplest form of subject-following and works well when the subject moves laterally past the camera at a moderate distance. It is commonly used in **sports coverage, surveillance-style sequences, and any scene where the camera cannot or should not physically move**. The technique keeps the subject framed without revealing depth or parallax.

- Related: [Tilt Tracking Shot](taxonomy:51) | [Pan Left](taxonomy:8) | [Pan Right](taxonomy:10)
tutorial.zh:
# 摇镜跟踪

相机通过摇镜来跟踪移动的主体。相机保持在固定位置不动，仅通过**水平旋转跟随主体的运动**轨迹。

摇镜跟踪是最简单的主体跟随方式，适用于主体在中等距离处横向经过相机的场景。该技法常用于**体育赛事转播、监控风格的影像，以及相机无法或不宜进行物理移动的场景**。由于相机不进行位移，该技法不会揭示深度或产生视差。

- 相关: [俯仰跟踪](taxonomy:51) | [摇镜左](taxonomy:8) | [摇镜右](taxonomy:10)

tutorial.en:
# Tilt Tracking Shot

The camera tilts to track the moving subjects. The camera stays in one position and **rotates vertically to follow the subject** as they move up or down in the frame.

Tilt tracking is used when a subject ascends stairs, climbs a wall, jumps, or falls. It can also follow a subject rising from seated to standing. The technique is simpler than a crane or pedestal move but effective for **maintaining focus on vertical motion without requiring physical camera displacement**.

- Related: [Pan Tracking Shot](taxonomy:45) | [Tilt Up](taxonomy:20) | [Tilt Down](taxonomy:18)
tutorial.zh:
# 俯仰跟踪

相机通过俯仰来跟踪移动的主体。相机保持在固定位置不动，仅通过**垂直旋转跟随主体的上下运动**。

俯仰跟踪用于主体上楼梯、攀爬墙壁、跳跃或坠落等场景，也可以跟随主体从坐姿到站立的过程。该技法比起重机或升降运动更简单，但在**保持对垂直运动的关注同时无需相机物理位移**方面十分有效。

- 相关: [摇镜跟踪](taxonomy:45) | [上仰](taxonomy:20) | [下俯](taxonomy:18)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Getting Larger

The subject appears larger during the tracking shot. As the camera tracks a subject, the subject's size in frame **increases over the duration of the shot**, indicating the camera is closing the distance or the subject is approaching.

This technique builds **intensity, intimacy, or confrontation**. A tracking shot where the subject steadily grows larger can create a sense of the audience being drawn into the subject's world, or of tension escalating as the camera pushes in during pursuit or approach.

- Related: [Subject Getting Smaller](taxonomy:54) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体变大

跟踪镜头中主体在画面中逐渐变大。随着相机跟踪主体，主体在画面中的占比**持续增大**，表明相机正在缩短距离或主体正在靠近。

这种技法增强**紧张感、亲密感或对抗感**。跟踪镜头中主体持续变大可以营造观众被拉入主体世界的感觉，或在追逐或接近场景中让张力不断升级。

- 相关: [主体变小](taxonomy:54) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Getting Smaller

The subject appears smaller during the tracking shot. As the camera tracks a subject, the subject's size in frame **decreases over the duration**, indicating the camera is falling behind or the subject is moving away.

This creates a sense of **separation, loss, or helplessness**. A shrinking subject during a tracking shot can convey abandonment, a character's isolation, or the futility of pursuit.

- Related: [Subject Getting Larger](taxonomy:53) | [Tracking Shot](taxonomy:52)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体变小

跟踪镜头中主体在画面中逐渐变小。随着相机跟踪主体，主体在画面中的占比**持续减小**，表明相机正在落后或主体正在远离。

这营造出**分离感、失落感或无助感**。跟踪镜头中不断缩小的主体可以传达被抛弃、角色的孤立，或追逐的徒劳。

- 相关: [主体变大](taxonomy:53) | [跟踪镜头](taxonomy:52)

tutorial.en:
# Front-Side Tracking Shot

A front-side tracking shot where the camera leads the moving subject from a front-side angle. The camera is positioned ahead and to one side of the subject, showing a three-quarter front view as they move forward.

This angle provides a **compromise between the intimacy of a lead shot and the spatial context of a side shot**. The subject's face is partially visible, and the viewer can see both where the subject is heading and how the environment unfolds beside them. It is common in action films and documentary-style shooting.

- Related: [Rear-Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:46) | [Lead Tracking Shot](taxonomy:44)
tutorial.zh:
# 前侧跟踪

前侧跟踪镜头中，相机从前侧角度引领移动的主体。相机位于主体前方偏侧的位置，展示四分之三正面视角。

这一角度提供了**前引镜头的亲密感与侧面镜头的空间感之间的折中**。主体的面部部分可见，观众既能看到主体前进的方向，也能看到环境在旁边展开。该角度在动作片和纪录片式拍摄中常见。

- 相关: [后侧跟踪](taxonomy:46) | [前引跟踪](taxonomy:44)

tutorial.en:
# Rear-Side Tracking Shot

A rear-side tracking shot where the camera follows the moving subject at a rear-side angle. The camera is positioned behind and to one side of the subject, showing a three-quarter rear view.

This angle offers a **sense of shadowing the character** while still revealing some environment ahead. It is frequently used in **pursuit sequences and stealth scenarios**, where the camera's oblique rear position mimics the feeling of someone trailing the subject.

- Related: [Front-Side Tracking Shot](taxonomy:43) | [Follow Tracking Shot](taxonomy:50)
tutorial.zh:
# 后侧跟踪

后侧跟踪镜头中，相机从后侧角度跟随移动的主体。相机位于主体后方偏侧的位置，展示四分之三背面视角。

这一角度营造出**尾随角色**的感觉，同时仍能揭示前方的部分环境。该角度常用于**追逐场景和潜行情节**，相机的斜后方位置模拟了有人在暗中跟踪主体的感觉。

- 相关: [前侧跟踪](taxonomy:43) | [后随跟踪](taxonomy:50)

tutorial.en: A side tracking shot where the camera moves left to follow the subject.
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪（向左）

侧面跟踪镜头中，相机向左移动以跟随主体。相机从主体的左侧进行横向平移。

- 相关: [侧面跟踪（向右）](taxonomy:49) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en: A side tracking shot where the camera moves right to follow the subject.
tutorial.zh:
# 侧面跟踪（向右）

侧面跟踪镜头中，相机向右移动以跟随主体。相机从主体的右侧进行横向平移。

- 相关: [侧面跟踪（向左）](taxonomy:48) | [侧面跟踪](taxonomy:47)

tutorial.en:
# Human Shot

A shot that primarily focuses on human subjects. The frame is composed around one or more people, making their actions, expressions, or body language the visual center of attention.

Human-focused shots form the foundation of narrative filmmaking, where **character and performance drive storytelling**. The specific way humans are framed (close-up for emotion, wide for context) shapes how the audience connects with the characters on screen.

- Related: [Non-Human Shot](taxonomy:220) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 人物镜头

主要聚焦于人物主体的镜头。画面围绕一个或多个人物构图，将其动作、表情或肢体语言作为视觉中心。

以人物为焦点的镜头是叙事电影的基础，其中**角色和表演驱动着故事**。人物的具体构图方式（特写传达情感，远景提供背景）决定了观众与银幕上角色的连接方式。

- 相关: [非人物镜头](taxonomy:220) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Non-Human Shot

A shot that primarily focuses on non-human subjects. The frame centers on animals, objects, vehicles, food, architecture, or other non-human elements as the primary visual subject.

Non-human shots are essential in **nature documentaries, product cinematography, food films, and sci-fi** where technology or environment serves as a character. They also appear in narrative films as insert shots that draw attention to symbolic objects or environmental details.

- Related: [Human Shot](taxonomy:208) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 非人物镜头

主要聚焦于非人物主体的镜头。画面以动物、物体、车辆、食物、建筑或其他非人物元素为主要视觉主体。

非人物镜头在**自然纪录片、产品摄影、美食影片和科幻片**中不可或缺，其中技术或环境本身就是「角色」。在叙事影片中，非人物镜头也作为插入镜头出现，将观众的注意力引向具有象征意义的物体或环境细节。

- 相关: [人物镜头](taxonomy:208) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Scenery Shot

The video shows scenery or environment without focusing on any subjects. No distinct subject dominates the frame; instead, the **landscape, cityscape, architecture, or atmospheric setting** fills the composition.

Scenery shots serve as **establishing shots, transitional breathers, or mood-setting interludes**. They give the audience spatial context and emotional tone. In the films of Terrence Malick and David Lean, expansive scenery shots carry as much narrative weight as character close-ups.

- Related: [Extreme Wide](taxonomy:188) | [Wide](taxonomy:193)
tutorial.zh:
# 风景镜头

展示风景或环境，不聚焦于任何特定主体。画面中没有突出的主体占据主导地位，取而代之的是**景观、城市全貌、建筑或氛围化的场景设定**填满整个构图。

风景镜头用作**建立镜头、过渡性间歇或情绪渲染插入**，为观众提供空间背景和情感基调。在泰伦斯·马力克和大卫·里恩的影片中，宏大的风景镜头承载着与角色特写同等的叙事分量。

- 相关: [超远景](taxonomy:188) | [远景](taxonomy:193)

tutorial.en:
# Multi-Subject (No Focus)

The video features multiple subjects in focus, with no single subject standing out as dominant. Several subjects share the frame with roughly **equal visual weight**, and the composition does not clearly prioritize one over the others.

This framing is used in **ensemble scenes, crowd shots, group portraits, and documentary coverage** where the relationships between subjects matter more than any individual. It can convey community, chaos, or democratic equality among characters.

- Related: [Multi-Subject (Single Focus)](taxonomy:216) | [Many Subjects](taxonomy:221)
tutorial.zh:
# 多主体（无焦点）

视频中有多个主体同时出现在画面中，且没有单一主体作为主导。多个主体以大致**相同的视觉分量**共享画面，构图并未明确将某一主体置于优先位置。

这种构图方式用于**群戏、人群场景、集体肖像和纪实拍摄**等场景，其中主体之间的关系比任何单一个体更为重要。它可以传达群体感、混乱感或角色之间的民主平等。

- 相关: [多主体（单焦点）](taxonomy:216) | [多个主体](taxonomy:221)

tutorial.en:
# Multi-Subject (Single Focus)

The video features multiple subjects, but one clearly stands out as the main focus. While several elements share the frame, **composition, focus, lighting, or placement** direct the viewer's eye to a single dominant subject.

This is the default approach in most narrative filmmaking: a character stands in a crowd, but depth of field or central framing isolates them. It allows filmmakers to **establish context while maintaining clear storytelling hierarchy**.

- Related: [Multi-Subject (No Focus)](taxonomy:215) | [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222)
tutorial.zh:
# 多主体（单焦点）

视频中有多个主体出现在画面中，但其中一个明显突出为主要焦点。虽然多个元素共享画面，但**构图、焦点、光线或位置安排**将观众的视线引向单一的主导主体。

这是大多数叙事电影的默认方式：一个角色站在人群中，但通过景深或居中构图被隔离出来。它使电影创作者能够**在建立背景的同时保持清晰的叙事层级**。

- 相关: [多主体（无焦点）](taxonomy:215) | [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222)

tutorial.en: The video includes a subject change, such as a revealing shot where a subject appears, or when a subject disappears or shifts to another.
The video features multiple salient subjects differing in type or framing, making it hard to classify the exact shot size.
The video has a clear subject with back-and-forth changes in shot size.
The video features a clear subject whose anatomy looks unnatural or exaggerated compared to real-world counterparts, making the exact shot size difficult to classify.
There is a clear subject, but the framing is unstable, making the exact shot size difficult to classify.
A video that consistently features one or two salient human subjects.
A video that consistently features one or two salient non-human subjects.
The video features a subject and scene that do not match in framing, making it hard to classify the shot size.

# Extreme Close Up

The video maintains an extreme close-up shot, consistently isolating a very small detail of the subject or scene. An **ECU** fills the frame with a tiny portion of the subject, such as an eye, a finger on a trigger, or a drop of sweat.

ECUs create **maximum intimacy and intensity**. They force the audience to confront a single detail with nowhere else to look. Sergio Leone's extreme close-ups of eyes during standoffs in [*The Good, the Bad and the Ugly* (1966)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly) are among cinema's most iconic uses of this shot size.

- Related: [Close Up](taxonomy:186)
tutorial.zh:
# 超特写

视频全程保持超特写景别，持续隔离主体或场景的极小细节。**超特写**（ECU）用主体的微小局部——如一只眼睛、扣动扳机的手指或一滴汗珠——充满整个画面。

超特写创造**最大程度的亲密感和视觉冲击力**，迫使观众直面某个细节而无处回避。塞尔吉奥·莱昂内在[《黄金三镖客》(1966)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good,_the_Bad_and_the_Ugly)对决场景中的眼部超特写是影史上该景别最具标志性的运用。

- 相关: [特写](taxonomy:186)

tutorial.en:
# Close Up

The video maintains a close-up shot, highlighting a distinct part of the subject or scene while still preserving some surrounding context. A **CU** typically shows a character's full face or an object filling most of the frame.

Close-ups are the workhorse of emotional storytelling, used to **capture subtle facial expressions, reactions, and intimate moments**. They create a direct emotional connection between the character and the audience. Alfred Hitchcock called the close-up one of cinema's most powerful tools for controlling audience attention.

- Related: [Extreme Close Up](taxonomy:187) | [Medium Close Up](taxonomy:191)
tutorial.zh:
# 特写

视频全程保持特写景别，突出主体的独特部分，同时保留少量周围环境。**特写**（CU）通常展示角色的整张面部或一个占据画面大部分区域的物体。

特写是情感叙事的核心工具，用于**捕捉细微的面部表情、反应和亲密时刻**，在角色与观众之间建立直接的情感连接。阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克将特写称为电影最强大的控制观众注意力的工具之一。

- 相关: [超特写](taxonomy:187) | [中近景](taxonomy:191)

tutorial.en:
# Medium Close Up

The video maintains a medium close-up shot, framing the human subject from the chest upward. An **MCU** balances **facial detail with enough body language** to show gestures and posture.

This is the standard framing for **TV interviews, news anchors, video calls, and dialogue scenes** where both expression and upper-body movement matter. It is close enough for emotional connection but wide enough to show hand gestures and the relationship between characters in over-the-shoulder setups.

- Related: [Close Up](taxonomy:186) | [Medium](taxonomy:190)
tutorial.zh:
# 中近景

视频全程保持中近景，画面显示人物主体从胸部以上。**中近景**（MCU）兼顾**面部细节和足够的肢体语言**，能够展示手势和体态。

这是**电视访谈、新闻主播、视频通话和对话场景**的标准构图，既足够近以建立情感连接，又足够宽以展示手部动作和过肩构图中角色之间的关系。

- 相关: [特写](taxonomy:186) | [中景](taxonomy:190)

tutorial.en:
# Medium

The video maintains a medium shot, framing about half of the human subject. A **MS** typically shows a person from roughly the waist up, providing a **balance between character detail and environmental context**.

The medium shot is the most versatile and commonly used shot size in narrative filmmaking. It is wide enough to show blocking and body language, yet close enough to read facial expressions. Classical Hollywood filmmaking relies heavily on medium shots for dialogue coverage.

- Related: [Medium Close Up](taxonomy:191) | [Medium Full](taxonomy:192)
tutorial.zh:
# 中景

视频全程保持中景，画面显示人物主体大约一半的身体。**中景**（MS）通常展示人物从大约腰部以上，提供**角色细节与环境背景之间的平衡**。

中景是叙事电影中最通用、最常用的景别。它既足够宽以展示调度和肢体语言，又足够近以读取面部表情。经典好莱坞电影在对话覆盖中大量依赖中景。

- 相关: [中近景](taxonomy:191) | [中全景](taxonomy:192)

tutorial.en:
# Medium Full

The video maintains a medium full shot, framing the human subject from mid-thigh (or knee) upward. Also called a **cowboy shot** or **American shot**, this framing became famous in Westerns where it was essential to show a gunslinger's holstered weapon at the hip.

The medium full shot provides **more body context than a standard medium** while keeping the subject large enough to read expressions. It is used in **action scenes, fashion photography, and any scenario where the subject's full stance or outfit matters**.

- Related: [Medium](taxonomy:190) | [Full](taxonomy:189)
tutorial.zh:
# 中全景

视频全程保持中全景，画面显示人物从大腿中部（或膝盖）以上。又称**牛仔镜头**（Cowboy Shot）或**美式镜头**（American Shot），这一构图方式在西部片中声名鹊起，因为在当时必须展示枪手腰间佩戴的武器。

中全景比标准中景提供**更多的身体信息**，同时保持主体足够大以读取表情。它用于**动作场景、时装摄影，以及任何主体完整站姿或服装造型至关重要的场景**。

- 相关: [中景](taxonomy:190) | [全景](taxonomy:189)

tutorial.en:
# Full

The video maintains a full shot, framing the entire body of the salient subject without showing excessive surrounding scenery. A **FS** contains the subject from head to toe with minimal extra space.

Full shots emphasize **physicality, body language, costume, and movement**. They are essential for **dance sequences, fight choreography, and any scene where full-body action tells the story**. In character introductions, a full shot reveals everything about a figure's appearance at once.

- Related: [Medium Full](taxonomy:192) | [Wide](taxonomy:193)
tutorial.zh:
# 全景

视频全程保持全景，完整展示主体从头到脚，不展示过多周围环境。**全景**（FS）以最小的额外空间包含主体全身。

全景强调**体态、肢体语言、服装和动作**。它在**舞蹈编排、格斗动作，以及任何全身表演传递故事信息的场景**中不可或缺。在角色介绍中，全景可以一次性揭示人物外形的一切信息。

- 相关: [中全景](taxonomy:192) | [远景](taxonomy:193)

tutorial.en:
# Wide

The video maintains a wide shot, consistently showing wide scenery or framing the entire body of the salient subject with ample background context. A **WS** (or **long shot**) shows the subject within their broader environment.

Wide shots establish the **spatial relationship between characters and their surroundings**. They serve as establishing shots, provide breathing room in editing, and allow the audience to absorb the full geography of a scene. Directors like David Lean and John Ford used wide shots of landscapes as visual poetry.

- Related: [Full](taxonomy:189) | [Extreme Wide](taxonomy:188)
tutorial.zh:
# 远景

视频全程保持远景，展示广阔场景或在充足的背景环境中完整展示主体。**远景**（WS，又称长镜头 Long Shot）展示主体及其更广阔的环境。

远景建立**主体与环境之间的空间关系**。它用作建立镜头、在剪辑中提供视觉「呼吸空间」，并让观众充分了解场景的完整地理信息。大卫·里恩和约翰·福特将景色远景运用为视觉诗歌。

- 相关: [全景](taxonomy:189) | [超远景](taxonomy:188)

tutorial.en:
# Extreme Wide

The video maintains an extreme wide shot, consistently emphasizing the vast environment over any subjects. An **EWS** (or **extreme long shot**) makes any human figures tiny against a dominating landscape or cityscape.

Extreme wide shots convey **scale, isolation, grandeur, or insignificance**. They are signature shots in epics, science fiction, and nature documentaries. The opening shot of [*Lawrence of Arabia* (1962)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_of_Arabia_(film)), showing a tiny figure against an endless desert, exemplifies the EWS's power to communicate the vastness of the world.

- Related: [Wide](taxonomy:193) | [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218)
tutorial.zh:
# 超远景

视频全程保持超远景，广阔环境占绝对主导地位。**超远景**（EWS，又称极远镜头 Extreme Long Shot）使画面中的任何人物都显得微小，被庞大的景观或城市全貌所吞没。

超远景传达**规模感、孤立感、宏伟感或渺小感**。它是史诗片、科幻片和自然纪录片的标志性镜头。[《阿拉伯的劳伦斯》(1962)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_of_Arabia_(film))的开场镜头——一个微小的身影置身于无尽沙漠之中——完美诠释了超远景传达世界浩瀚的力量。

- 相关: [远景](taxonomy:193) | [风景镜头](taxonomy:218)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change

The shot size changes noticeably during the video. The framing shifts between different shot sizes (e.g., from wide to close-up) **within a single continuous shot**, rather than through editing cuts.

In-shot size changes create **dynamic visual storytelling without cutting**. A dolly-in from wide to close-up can build emotional intensity, while a pull-out from close-up to wide can reveal surprising context. These continuous transitions feel more organic than jump cuts and maintain temporal continuity.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Large → Small)](taxonomy:195) | [Shot Size Change (Small → Large)](taxonomy:196)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别变化

视频中景别有明显变化。画面构图在**单个连续镜头内**从一种景别转换到另一种景别（例如从远景到特写），而非通过剪辑切换。

镜头内的景别变化创造**动态的视觉叙事而无需剪切**。从远景推入特写可以不断增强情感强度，而从特写拉出至远景则可以揭示出人意料的环境背景。这种连续性的过渡比跳切更具有机感，并维持了时间的连续性。

- 相关: [景别从大变小](taxonomy:195) | [景别从小变大](taxonomy:196)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change (Large → Small)

The shot size changes noticeably from a wider to a tighter framing. The camera or zoom moves in during the shot, transitioning from a broader view to a more intimate one.

This progression **builds emotional intensity, narrows the audience's focus, and creates a sense of closing in** on the subject. It is a natural way to transition from establishing context to isolating a key detail or expression.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Small → Large)](taxonomy:196) | [Zoom In](taxonomy:22) | [Dolly Forward](taxonomy:35)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别从大变小

景别从较宽的构图明显转变为较紧的构图。相机或变焦在拍摄过程中推进，从更广的视野过渡到更亲密的画面。

这种进程**增强情感强度、收窄观众的注意力，并营造逐渐逼近的感觉**。它是从建立背景到聚焦关键细节或表情的自然过渡方式。

- 相关: [景别从小变大](taxonomy:196) | [变焦推进](taxonomy:22) | [推轨前进](taxonomy:35)

tutorial.en:
# Shot Size Change (Small → Large)

The shot size changes noticeably from a tighter to a wider framing. The camera or zoom pulls back during the shot, revealing more of the environment.

This progression **creates reveals, builds context, or generates a sense of expanding perspective**. A classic example is a close-up that widens to show the character is actually in a surprising or dangerous location.

- Related: [Shot Size Change (Large → Small)](taxonomy:195) | [Zoom Out](taxonomy:24) | [Dolly Backward](taxonomy:29)
tutorial.zh:
# 景别从小变大

景别从较紧的构图明显转变为较宽的构图。相机或变焦在拍摄过程中拉远，揭示更多的周围环境。

这种进程**创造揭示效果、建立背景，或营造视角不断扩展的感觉**。经典用法是从特写逐渐拉宽，揭示角色实际上身处一个出人意料或危险的环境之中。

- 相关: [景别从大变小](taxonomy:195) | [变焦拉远](taxonomy:24) | [推轨后退](taxonomy:29)

# Single Dominant Subject

A video that maintains a single or two dominant subjects throughout. The composition consistently centers on **one or two clearly identifiable subjects** that command the viewer's attention.

Single-subject framing is the backbone of **character-driven storytelling, portraits, product shots, and interview setups**. Maintaining a consistent subject allows the audience to build a sustained connection.

- Related: [Many Subjects](taxonomy:221) | [Framing Subject](taxonomy:224)
tutorial.zh:
# 单一主导主体

视频全程保持一个或两个主导主体。构图始终以**一到两个清晰可辨的主体**为中心，吸引并维持观众的注意力。

单一主体构图是**角色驱动叙事、人物肖像、产品拍摄和访谈设置**的基础。维持稳定的主体让观众能建立持续的情感连接。

- 相关: [多个主体](taxonomy:221) | [有构图主体](taxonomy:224)

tutorial.en:
# Many Subjects

The video either shows three or more main subjects in clear focus, or shifts focus from one subject to another. Multiple subjects share visual prominence, and the frame accommodates their **collective presence or sequential attention**.

Many-subject framing is used in **group scenes, ensemble casts, crowd coverage, and multi-character interactions**. Managing visual attention across multiple subjects is one of the key challenges of composition.

- Related: [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222) | [Multi-Subject (No Focus)](taxonomy:215)
tutorial.zh:
# 多个主体

视频中显示三个或更多主要主体同时清晰可见，或焦点在不同主体之间转移。多个主体共享视觉突出地位，画面容纳其**集体存在或依次关注**。

多主体构图用于**群戏、合奏阵容、人群拍摄和多人互动场景**。在多个主体之间管理视觉注意力是构图的关键挑战之一。

- 相关: [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222) | [多主体（无焦点）](taxonomy:215)

tutorial.en:
# Framing Subject

The video includes one or more salient subjects in the frame at any point. At least one **identifiable subject** (human, animal, object, or vehicle) appears and serves as a focal point for the composition.

This is a broad classification distinguishing shots that feature identifiable subjects from pure scenery or abstract imagery. Most narrative and documentary footage contains a framing subject.

- Related: [Scenery Shot](taxonomy:218) | [Single Dominant Subject](taxonomy:222)
tutorial.zh:
# 有构图主体

视频中至少有一个可辨认的主体（人物、动物、物体或车辆）出现并作为构图焦点。至少有一个**可识别的主体**在某一时刻出现在画面中。

这是一个宽泛的分类，区分包含可辨主体的镜头与纯风景或抽象画面。大多数叙事和纪录片素材都包含构图主体。

- 相关: [风景镜头](taxonomy:218) | [单一主导主体](taxonomy:222)

tutorial.en: The subject changes in the video, such as appearing, disappearing, or transitioning to another subject.

# Subject Disappearing

The video shows the main subject disappearing or leaving the frame. The subject **exits the visible area** by walking out, being obscured, or receding beyond visibility during the shot.

Subject disappearance creates **narrative tension, closure, or mystery**. A character walking out of frame can signal departure or defiance. An object fading from view can convey loss. The empty frame left behind often carries powerful emotional weight.

- Related: [Subject Revealing](taxonomy:206) | [Subject Switch](taxonomy:207)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体消失

视频中主要主体消失或离开画面。主体通过走出画面、被遮挡或退至不可见的远处而**退出可见区域**。

主体消失创造**叙事张力、结束感或神秘感**。角色走出画面可以暗示离去或反抗；物体从视野中消失可以传达失去。留下的空画面往往承载着强大的情感重量。

- 相关: [主体出现](taxonomy:206) | [主体切换](taxonomy:207)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Revealing

A revealing shot where the subject comes into view on screen. The subject **enters or becomes visible** during the shot, either by walking into frame, being uncovered by camera movement, or emerging from obscurity.

Revealing shots build **anticipation and surprise**. Delaying the subject's appearance creates tension; when the reveal finally occurs, it carries extra visual and narrative impact. This technique is fundamental to character introductions, plot twists, and dramatic reveals.

- Related: [Subject Disappearing](taxonomy:205) | [Subject Switch](taxonomy:207)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体出现

揭示性镜头中，主体在画面中进入视野或变得可见。主体通过走入画面、被相机运动揭示或从模糊中浮现而**出现或变得可见**。

揭示性镜头营造**期待感和惊喜感**。延迟主体的出现会制造张力；当揭示最终发生时，它承载着额外的视觉和叙事冲击力。这一技法是角色介绍、剧情反转和戏剧性揭示的基础。

- 相关: [主体消失](taxonomy:205) | [主体切换](taxonomy:207)

tutorial.en:
# Subject Switch

The main subject changes to another subject. The video's focal point **transitions from one subject to a different one** during the shot, without a cut.

Subject switching within a continuous shot demonstrates **directorial control over audience attention**. It can redirect focus during a conversation, shift from a person to an object they are looking at, or transition between characters in a complex blocking arrangement. Rack focus is one common technique for achieving subject switches.

- Related: [Subject Revealing](taxonomy:206) | [Subject Disappearing](taxonomy:205) | [Rack Focus](taxonomy:109)
tutorial.zh:
# 主体切换

主要主体变换为另一个主体。视频的焦点在拍摄过程中从一个主体**过渡到另一个不同的主体**，且未经剪切。

连续镜头内的主体切换展现了**导演对观众注意力的控制**。它可以在对话中重新引导焦点，将注意力从一个人物转向其注视的物体，或在复杂场面调度中完成角色之间的过渡。变焦拉焦是实现主体切换的常用技法之一。

- 相关: [主体出现](taxonomy:206) | [主体消失](taxonomy:205) | [变焦拉焦](taxonomy:109)

tutorial.en:
# Bird's Eye

The camera maintains a bird's eye angle throughout, consistently looking straight down from above. A **bird's eye view** (or **top-down shot**) positions the camera directly overhead, perpendicular to the ground.

This extreme overhead perspective **flattens depth, transforms familiar scenes into abstract patterns, and provides an omniscient vantage point**. It can convey surveillance, divine perspective, or visual abstraction. Busby Berkeley's kaleidoscopic overhead shots of synchronized dancers in 1930s musicals remain iconic examples.

With drones, bird's eye shots have become far more common, revealing geometric patterns in cityscapes, nature, and human gatherings.

- Related: [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Overhead POV](taxonomy:169) | [Worm's Eye](taxonomy:80)
tutorial.zh:
# 鸟瞰

相机全程保持鸟瞰角度，从正上方直视下方。**鸟瞰**（又称俯拍镜头）将相机置于正上方，与地面垂直。

这种极端的俯视视角**将深度压平，将熟悉的场景转化为抽象图案，并提供全知的观察视点**。它可以传达监视感、神的视角或视觉抽象。巴斯比·伯克利在1930年代音乐片中以万花筒般的俯拍群舞编排创造了最具标志性的鸟瞰镜头。

随着无人机的普及，鸟瞰镜头变得更加常见，揭示出城市风貌、自然景观和人群聚集中肉眼不可见的几何图案。

- 相关: [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [俯视视角](taxonomy:169) | [虫视](taxonomy:80)

tutorial.en:
# High Angle

The camera maintains a high angle throughout, consistently looking downward compared to a level angle but not directly top-down. The camera is elevated above the subject and tilted down.

High angles make subjects appear **smaller, weaker, vulnerable, or dominated by their environment**. This psychological effect is widely used in thriller and horror films to suggest powerlessness. Conversely, high angles can provide a clear overview of spatial layouts, making them useful for **action choreography and establishing geography**.

- Related: [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76) | [Level Angle](taxonomy:78) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 高角度

相机全程保持高角度，从上方向下看，但并非正上方俯视。相机位于主体上方并向下倾斜。

高角度使主体显得**更小、更弱、更脆弱，或被环境所支配**。这一心理效果在惊悚片和恐怖片中被广泛运用，以暗示无力感。同时，高角度也能提供清晰的空间布局概览，使其对于**动作编排和地理建立**十分实用。

- 相关: [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76) | [水平角度](taxonomy:78) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Level Angle

The camera maintains a level angle parallel to the ground (even if a Dutch angle is used) throughout the video. The lens points horizontally, matching the natural human eye line.

Level angle is the **neutral, default camera angle** that feels natural and unmanipulated. It places the viewer at the same plane as the action, creating a sense of **objectivity and equality** with the subjects. Most dialogue scenes, interviews, and everyday coverage use level angles as their baseline.

- Related: [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 水平角度

相机全程保持与地面平行的水平角度（即使使用了荷兰角）。镜头水平朝向前方，与人眼的自然视线一致。

水平角度是**默认的中性相机角度**，给人以自然、不受操控的感受。它将观众置于与场中动作相同的平面上，营造出**客观性和与主体平等关系**的感觉。大多数对话场景、访谈和日常拍摄都以水平角度作为基准。

- 相关: [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Low Angle

The camera maintains a low angle throughout, consistently looking upward compared to a level angle but not directly bottom-up. The camera is positioned below the subject and tilted up.

Low angles make subjects appear **larger, more powerful, imposing, or heroic**. This is one of cinema's most effective tools for conveying dominance or authority. Orson Welles famously used extreme low angles in [*Citizen Kane* (1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane) to emphasize Charles Foster Kane's towering ego, even building sets with ceilings to accommodate the perspective.

- Related: [Level Angle](taxonomy:78) | [Worm's Eye](taxonomy:80) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77)
tutorial.zh:
# 低角度

相机全程保持低角度，从下方向上看，但并非正下方仰视。相机位于主体下方并向上倾斜。

低角度使主体显得**更高大、更有力、更具威慑感或英雄气概**。这是电影中传达支配力或权威感最有效的工具之一。奥逊·威尔斯在[《公民凯恩》(1941)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_Kane)中大量使用极低角度来强调查尔斯·福斯特·凯恩膨胀的自我，甚至为配合这一视角特意搭建了带天花板的布景。

- 相关: [水平角度](taxonomy:78) | [虫视](taxonomy:80) | [高角度](taxonomy:77)

tutorial.en:
# Worm's Eye

The camera maintains a worm's eye angle throughout, consistently looking straight up from below. A **worm's eye view** positions the camera at ground level (or below) and points directly upward.

This extreme upward perspective creates maximum **distortion, grandeur, and visual drama**. Buildings tower infinitely, characters loom like giants, and ceilings become the dominant visual element. It is used sparingly for **stylized impact, surreal sequences, or to convey an insect-like or child-like ground-level perspective**.

- Related: [Low Angle](taxonomy:79) | [Bird's Eye](taxonomy:76)
tutorial.zh:
# 虫视

相机全程从正下方直视上方。**虫视**将相机置于地面（或更低处），镜头直指天空。

这种极端的仰视视角创造最大程度的**透视扭曲、宏伟感和视觉冲击力**。建筑无限高耸，人物如巨人般矗立，天花板成为画面的主导元素。虫视因其强烈的视觉效果而被谨慎使用，多见于**风格化镜头、超现实场景或表现虫类和儿童视角的地面视角**。

- 相关: [低角度](taxonomy:79) | [鸟瞰](taxonomy:76)

tutorial.en:
# Dutch Angle

There is an obvious Dutch (canted) angle (more than 15 degrees) that occurs in the video. A **Dutch angle** (or **Dutch tilt**, **canted angle**) rotates the camera so the horizon line is no longer level, creating a diagonal composition.

The Dutch angle conveys **unease, tension, disorientation, or psychological instability**. It originated in German Expressionist cinema of the 1920s (hence "Deutsch angle") and has been used extensively in **film noir, horror, and comic book adaptations**. Tim Burton, Sam Raimi, and the cinematography of [*The Third Man* (1949)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Third_Man) are known for prominent Dutch angles.

Overuse of the Dutch angle is considered a hallmark of amateur filmmaking, so it is typically deployed deliberately for specific narrative effect.

- Related: [Dutch Angle (Varying)](taxonomy:83) | [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16)
tutorial.zh:
# 荷兰角

视频中出现明显的荷兰角（倾斜角度超过15度）且角度保持不变。**荷兰角**（Dutch Angle，又称 Dutch Tilt 或 Canted Angle）将相机旋转使地平线不再水平，创造出对角线构图。

荷兰角传达**不安、紧张、迷失方向感或心理不稳定**。它起源于1920年代德国表现主义电影（因此得名「Deutsch Angle」），在**黑色电影、恐怖片和漫画改编影片**中被广泛使用。蒂姆·波顿、山姆·雷米以及[《第三人》(1949)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Third_Man)的摄影风格都以突出的荷兰角闻名。

荷兰角的过度使用被视为业余电影制作的标志，因此通常被刻意且有节制地用于特定的叙事效果。

- 相关: [变化荷兰角](taxonomy:83) | [顺时针横滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针横滚](taxonomy:16)

tutorial.en: There is an obvious Dutch (canted) angle (more than 15 degrees) that occurs in the video.

# Angle Change

The camera angle changes significantly relative to the ground, moving between bird's eye, high angle, level, low angle, or worm's eye view. The **tilt orientation of the camera shifts** during the shot.

Angle changes within a single shot create **dynamic visual progression** without cutting. A shot that begins at high angle and transitions to level can shift the audience's psychological relationship with the subject from dominance to equality.

- Related: [Angle Change (High → Low)](taxonomy:63) | [Angle Change (Low → High)](taxonomy:64)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度变化

相机角度相对地面发生显著变化，在鸟瞰、高角度、水平、低角度或虫视之间转换。相机的**俯仰朝向在拍摄过程中发生移动**。

单个镜头内的角度变化创造**动态的视觉进程而无需剪切**。从高角度起始过渡到水平角度，可以将观众与主体的心理关系从支配转变为平等。

- 相关: [角度从高到低](taxonomy:63) | [角度从低到高](taxonomy:64)

tutorial.en:
# Angle Change (High → Low)

The camera angle decreases noticeably relative to the ground, moving from a higher angle toward a lower one. The camera transitions from looking down to looking more level or upward.

This shift can **empower the subject over the course of the shot**, visually representing a character gaining confidence, authority, or control. It is a subtle but effective way to chart a psychological shift within continuous footage.

- Related: [Angle Change (Low → High)](taxonomy:64) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度从高到低

相机角度相对地面明显降低，从较高的角度向较低的角度过渡。相机从向下看转变为更水平或向上看。

这一转变可以在镜头进行过程中**赋予主体力量**，视觉化地呈现角色获得信心、权威或控制力的过程。这是一种微妙但有效的方式，在连续画面中刻画心理转变。

- 相关: [角度从低到高](taxonomy:64) | [高角度](taxonomy:77) | [低角度](taxonomy:79)

tutorial.en:
# Angle Change (Low → High)

The camera angle increases noticeably relative to the ground, moving from a lower angle toward a higher one. The camera transitions from looking up to looking more level or downward.

This shift can **diminish the subject's perceived power**, suggesting a loss of status, growing vulnerability, or the audience gaining an overview perspective. It reverses the empowerment arc of a high-to-low transition.

- Related: [Angle Change (High → Low)](taxonomy:63) | [Low Angle](taxonomy:79) | [High Angle](taxonomy:77)
tutorial.zh:
# 角度从低到高

相机角度相对地面明显升高，从较低的角度向较高的角度过渡。相机从向上看转变为更水平或向下看。

这一转变可以**削弱主体的感知力量**，暗示地位的丧失、日益增长的脆弱感，或观众获得了俯瞰全局的视角。它反转了从高到低过渡的赋权弧线。

- 相关: [角度从高到低](taxonomy:63) | [低角度](taxonomy:79) | [高角度](taxonomy:77)

tutorial.en:
# Dutch Angle (Varying)

There is a Dutch (canted) angle that changes its degree during the video, with the horizon line not level. The **canted angle actively shifts**, becoming more or less extreme over the course of the shot.

A varying Dutch angle amplifies the sense of **instability and disorientation** beyond a static tilt. As the horizon continues to shift, the viewer's spatial anchoring is progressively undermined. This technique appears in dream sequences, intoxication scenes, and moments of extreme psychological distress.

- Related: [Dutch Angle](taxonomy:82) | [Roll Clockwise](taxonomy:14) | [Roll Counterclockwise](taxonomy:16)
tutorial.zh:
# 变化荷兰角

视频中荷兰角的倾斜角度在持续变化，地平线始终不水平。**倾斜角度主动移动**，在拍摄过程中变得更极端或更缓和。

变化的荷兰角将**不稳定感和迷失方向感**放大到静态倾斜无法企及的程度。随着地平线的持续偏移，观众的空间锚定被逐步瓦解。这种技法出现在梦境场景、醉酒画面和极端心理危机的时刻。

- 相关: [荷兰角](taxonomy:82) | [顺时针横滚](taxonomy:14) | [逆时针横滚](taxonomy:16)
